the_candidate.message: Bump SnakeYaml to 2.4 to remedieate CVE-2022-25857, CVE-2022-38749 (#107)
the_candidate.traversal: confirmed: direct 1.26 -> 2.4 in pom.xml, same commit as the adaptation
the_candidate.why_it_looked_strong: A dedicated bump commit -- not a feature PR -- touching exactly one production file, and that file references the library. The best-shaped open row in the codepointlimit corpus.

why_excluded.finding: A COMPILE break, and attributed to the wrong break. The adaptation responds to snakeyaml 2.0 removing the Constructor(Class) overload, not to the 1.32 code-point limit.
why_excluded.the_diff: `CustomConstructor(Class<?> theRoot) { super(theRoot); }` becomes `CustomConstructor() { super(new LoaderOptions()); }`, and the call site `new CustomConstructor(Configuration.class)` becomes `new CustomConstructor()`. The only other change is pinning the version to a ${snakeyaml.version} property.
why_excluded.why_it_is_a_compile_break: snakeyaml 2.0 removed every Constructor overload that does not take a LoaderOptions. `super(theRoot)` stops compiling, so the client never reaches any runtime behaviour change. State 2 would fail at javac.
why_excluded.wrong_break: The crossing 1.26 -> 2.4 passes through the 1.32 code-point boundary, which is why the codepointlimit mine caught it, but nothing in the diff touches setCodePointLimit or any limit. Crossing a boundary is not the same as adapting to it.
why_excluded.collateral_note: The fix also drops the root type: the constructor no longer receives Configuration.class. That is a semantic change made to satisfy the compiler, not to restore behaviour.
why_excluded.pattern: Fourth instance of the snakeyaml-2.0 constructor-removal compile break, after adityajoy-1902/Dashboard-V-2, snork-alt/beanszoo and GoogleCloudPlatform/appengine-plugins. The compile-masking assessment on snakeyaml-1.x-to-2.0 now stands at 4 for 4.
